verdict_text:
YES

The slicing logic matches the specification exactly. For both `query_key_value` tensors the index builder walks `6144 // 768 = 8` head blocks along dim 0 and skips block 5, yielding rows `0..3839` then `4608..6143` in order (shape `[5376, 2048]` and `[5376]`). For `attention.dense.weight` it walks `2048 // 256 = 8` blocks along dim 1 and skips block 5, yielding columns `0..1279` then `1536..2047` (shape `[2048, 1792]`). All 16 layers are covered, no other tensor is touched, names are preserved, `index_select` preserves float16, and all four required checks are asserted before `save_file` writes the single `out/T2/model.safetensors`.

One thing I could not verify from reading alone: the script delegates loading to a local `_ckpt.load_checkpoint` helper that was not provided, so the assumption that it returns the full 244-key float16 state dict unmodified rests on the `len(sd) == 244` assertion that does run before writing.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
